open_points.subject: Project
open_points.text: every operation on a project needs the token.
open_points.question: What is a Project, is it a value or entity, and who mints its identity from what source?
options: Project is an entity identified by a caller-supplied project ID
Project is an entity minted by the deliverer from a confirmed folder
Project is a value identified directly by its confirmed folder
open_points.default_guess: Project is an entity whose ID is supplied by the caller and whose confirmed source folder is an attribute.

witness.initial: A confirmed folder is moved to a new path while retaining the same content.
events: The caller scans the moved folder using the same project reference.
The deliverer determines which project the operation is on.
outcomes: The scan remains attached to the same project entity.
The folder path or folder-derived identity causes the scan to address a new project.
witness.observer: The caller and anyone viewing placements for the project

open_points.subject: token
open_points.text: every operation on a project needs the token.
open_points.question: What does “the token” identify, is it a value or entity, and who mints it from what source?
options: An opaque value minted outside the deliverer
A persistent credential entity minted and stored by the deliverer
A value derived from the project identity or confirmed folder
A Portal credential supplied by the caller
open_points.default_guess: It is an opaque non-Portal value minted by an external composition boundary and supplied to the deliverer.

witness.initial: A caller has a project ID, a confirmed folder and a Portal credential.
events: The caller invokes scan with a token.
The deliverer interprets the token according to its model.
outcomes: The token is an independent project-access capability and the Portal credential is irrelevant.
The Portal credential itself is accepted as the token despite the deliverer holding no Portal credential.
witness.observer: The caller and the security operator

open_points.subject: token-to-project relationship
open_points.text: every operation on a project needs the token.
open_points.question: Is a token bound to exactly one project, usable for a defined set of projects, or merely required without being project-bound?
options: Exactly one token-to-project binding
One token may authorize several projects
Any valid token authorizes operations on any project
open_points.default_guess: Each token is bound to exactly one project.

witness.initial: Projects A and B exist and the caller possesses the token used successfully for A.
events: The caller invokes scan for project B using A's token.
outcomes: The operation is rejected because the token is bound to A.
The operation proceeds because token validity is global or covers both projects.
witness.observer: The caller and the owner of project B

open_points.subject: scan, deliver and record-publication actions
open_points.text: The deliverer offers three operations: scan a project's folder, deliver one photo, and record its publication. When to scan, what to deliver next, what to repeat and which failure to treat as temporary belong to the calling flow. The guarantees stay in the service: source folders are only read, metadata is removed, only a confirmed folder is used, a repeated delivery creates nothing new, and every operation on a project needs the token.
open_points.question: Which of scan, deliver and record-publication count as operations “on a project” and therefore read and validate the token?
options: All three operations require the token
Only scan explicitly operates on a project and requires it
Scan and deliver require it, while recording publication does not
Whether an invocation requires it depends on whether that invocation carries a project reference
open_points.default_guess: All three operations require and validate the token against their project.

witness.initial: A photo has already been delivered for a project, but its publication has not been recorded.
events: The caller invokes record-publication without a token.
outcomes: Recording is rejected because it is one of the project's three operations.
Recording succeeds because publication recording is not defined as an operation on a project.
witness.observer: The caller and users relying on publication state

open_points.subject: token possession by the deliverer
open_points.text: every operation on a project needs the token.
open_points.question: Must every operation receive the token as invocation data, or may the deliverer retain it in project or session state between operations?
options: The caller supplies the token to every operation and the deliverer does not retain it
The token is stored with the project and read by later operations
The token is retained only for a bounded session
open_points.default_guess: The caller supplies the token to every operation and the deliverer does not retain it.

witness.initial: The caller successfully scans a project using a token.
events: The caller invokes deliver for the same project without resupplying the token.
outcomes: Delivery is rejected because each operation must receive the token.
Delivery succeeds because the earlier token was retained in project or session state.
witness.observer: The caller and the operator inspecting retained credentials

open_points.subject: token lifecycle
open_points.text: every operation on a project needs the token.
open_points.question: Does the token have lifecycle facts or statuses such as active, expired, rotated or revoked, and which product action changes them?
options: The token has no represented lifecycle; validity is external
The token is an entity with active and revoked statuses
The token is a value with expiry or rotation metadata
open_points.default_guess: Token validity and lifecycle are external; the deliverer only reads the supplied opaque value.

witness.initial: A token has previously authorized operations on a project.
events: An external authority rotates or revokes that token.
The caller repeats a project operation using the old token.
outcomes: The old token is rejected because revocation or rotation is represented and read.
The old token remains acceptable because the deliverer has no token lifecycle fact or status.
witness.observer: The caller and the project security owner
